svg.text: Trimbin — The Archive
ClickHouse holds what happened. Nothing in it is ever updated in place, which is the property the whole product rests on.
EVENTS · APPEND ONLY
Written once, never modified. MergeTree, partitioned by month.
clips
One row per piece of footage: measurements, slate
reading, findings with timecodes, description embedding
decisions
One row per take considered, with the reason recorded at
the time and who or what decided it
placements
Where a clip belongs. A correction appends a new row;
the mistaken one stays, which is how misfiling is auditable
clip_segments · clip_moments
Usable ranges and timecoded moments, per analysis run
finding_events · analysis_runs
What was flagged, what a person did about it, which run
coverage_selection_events
Editorial usage: which ranges stand for a shot
clip_lifecycle_events · activity · comments
Deletion and restoration, the audit trail, the conversation
READ MODELS · DERIVED
Views over the log. The current state is a question asked of history.
current_clip_placement
Where every clip stands right now. The one view every
operational screen reads, so there is one answer, not five
settled_placement
The last settled row per clip, resolved by
argMax over (occurred_at, event_id) — never ambiguous
placement_inbox · current_unassigned_clips
What is proposed and waiting, and what a person
deliberately left outside the structure
review_queue
Every shot still wanting a person, by one rule the
interface reads rather than re-deriving
accuracy · accuracy_by_project
Where a person overruled the recommendation, counted
from the log. Nothing is self-reported
real_clips · real_decisions
Synthetic rows are separated at the schema, so test data
cannot reach a figure anybody is shown
WHY THIS SHAPE
An edit decision is a fact, not a field
A row that is updated forgets. Six months on,
"why was take 4 chosen" has no answer if the
answer was overwritten by take 6. Every
decision, override and correction is a new row.
Mutations never touch a request
ALTER TABLE … UPDATE rewrites whole parts,
runs asynchronously and is capped in flight.
One in an interactive path is a screen that
hangs under load. There are none.
Reads are analytical, not transactional
"Every rejected take across four productions,
with its reason" is a column scan over
millions of rows. That is the query this
database is shaped for.
One store, three kinds of search
Structured filters, full-text over descriptions
and reasons, and vector similarity over
embeddings — in a single query, against one
table. No second system to keep in step.
HOW THE CURRENT STATE IS DERIVED
A clip is misfiled by the slate agent, corrected by an editor, then moved again after a conform. Three rows, in order:

text.tspan: placements scene 4 shot 2 take 3 source=slate state=open 2026-08-14 09:12:04.221
placements scene 4 shot 3 take 1 source=human state=settled 2026-08-14 11:40:57.883 "wrong setup, this is the reverse"
placements scene 4 shot 3 take 2 source=human state=settled 2026-08-19 16:02:11.104 "renumbered after the conform"

svg.text: All three rows remain. settled_placement answers "take 2" by argMax over (occurred_at, event_id) — deterministic even for two events in the same millisecond.

text.tspan: The mistaken reading is still there. Six months later, "which clips did the slate agent get wrong, and who corrected them" is a query, not an investigation —
and it is the same query that produces the published accuracy figure. Neither is calculated by the thing being measured.

svg.text: Amber: events, written once. Blue: views, computed on read. Nothing flows the other way.
